title: DeLELSTM block: level, slope and phase
summary: A Holt-style recurrence updates a level and slope on the prefix; its last slope extrapolates the trend afterward. The next step uses phase-wise means of the detrended prefix. The frames expose those buckets, their cumulative averages and the repeated seasonal output. The implemented trend is a level/slope recurrence with a phase template. No LSTM cell is trained or evaluated.

steps.title: Update level and slope
steps.text: A Holt-style recurrence updates a level and slope on the prefix; its last slope extrapolates the trend afterward.

steps.title: Average equal seasonal phases
steps.text: Subtract the trend on the fitting prefix. Group samples by index modulo the specified period and average each phase bucket.

steps.title: Repeat the phase template
steps.text: Tile the fitted phase means over the record. The suffix does not update the template in this prefix configuration.

steps.title: Inspect the derived residual
steps.text: Compute input minus the implemented trend and seasonal estimate. This residual is part of a retrospective decomposition, not a forecast score.

parameters.name: alpha / beta
parameters.effect: Control level and slope updates in the implemented Holt recurrence; no LSTM cell is evaluated.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Defines phase buckets in samples; the fitting prefix must contain enough cycles for an interpretable average.

parameters.name: fit_scope / train_fraction
parameters.effect: Explicitly selects a two-thirds prefix in this example; it does not create a rolling forecasting evaluation.

cautions: The implemented trend is a level/slope recurrence with a phase template. No LSTM cell is trained or evaluated.
Prefix fitting is a fixed fitting convention. It does not certify rolling causality or an out-of-sample prediction experiment.
A repeated phase template assumes that the fitted seasonal shape remains useful over the displayed suffix.
The residual is derived by subtraction; exact reconstruction does not validate the scientific interpretation of either component.

references.title: Wang et al. (2023), DeLELSTM: Decomposition-based Linear Explainable LSTM to Capture Instantaneous and Long-term Effects in Time Series

trace_note: Intermediate arrays are computed with the implemented operator helpers. The final trend, season and residual are checked against public decompose(). The animation explains this standalone experimental block; its source architecture is cited for provenance.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.

checks.validation_scope: One deterministic teaching input; no benchmark claim.
